root_cause.text: In nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg, the nfs4_file access count was unconditionally incremented via __nfs4_file_get_access before checking if the file already had a read file descriptor, leading to a double increment when the descriptor was already set by another thread.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the __nfs4_file_get_access call inside the `if (!fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY])` block, and the CVE description states: "if fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is already set by another thread, __nfs4_file_get_access should not be called to increment the nfs4_file access count since that was already done."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reference counting and delegation file assignment by only performing those operations when actually adding a new read-only file descriptor.
intent_record.what: Moved __nfs4_file_get_access and fp->fi_rdeleg_file assignment inside the if block that checks if fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is NULL, so they are only executed when a new read-only file descriptor is added.
intent_record.how: This prevents incrementing the file's access count and setting the delegation file reference when the file descriptor already exists, avoiding potential reference imbalances and incorrect delegation file assignments.

grouping_result.intent: Fix reference counting and delegation file assignment by only performing those operations when actually adding a new read-only file descriptor.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent directly aligns with the root cause by fixing the unconditional increment of the access count and delegation file assignment, ensuring they only happen when a new read-only file descriptor is added.

candidates.rationale: This line unconditionally increments the nfs4_file access count before checking if the read file descriptor is already set. If another thread has already set fi_fds[O_RDONLY], the access count is incremented twice, causing a reference count leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line unconditionally increments the nfs4_file access count before checking if the file already has a read file descriptor. If another thread has already set fi_fds[O_RDONLY], the access count is incremented twice, causing a double increment and reference count leak.
